name: Robbie Mahrou
bio: Robbie Mahrou is an independent candidate for New Hampshire's 2nd congressional district who lives in Walpole. Raised in Houston and a Baylor University graduate, he has worked in insurance, mortgage lending, film producing and talent management, and as an independent entrepreneur and consultant. He qualified for the November ballot by petition with more than 1,600 signatures.

platform.point: Backs a full audit of the Federal Reserve and matching any debt ceiling increase with spending cuts.
Supports faster federal permitting and returning zoning decisions to local communities.
Backs the PRIME Act and small-scale local meat and food processing infrastructure.
Proposes redirecting existing federal funds to a regional food production and processing hub in Grafton County.
Supports bills to preserve Critical Access hospital designations and to reduce mandates on small rural facilities.
Backs the National Constitutional Carry Act and opposes new federal restrictions on gun owners.
Calls for strict limits on federal AI surveillance and warrantless data collection.
Would repeal the 2001 AUMF and require congressional approval for sustained military action.

economy.evidence: Platform calls for Federal Reserve audit, deficit-matched debt ceiling increases, lighter regulation and ending corporate and agribusiness subsidies.

liberty.evidence: On guns he backs national constitutional carry and opposes new federal gun limits; on speech he backs the Free Speech Protection Act; abortion and drugs not addressed.

security.evidence: Platform calls for strict limits on federal AI surveillance and warrantless data collection.

foreign.evidence: Would repeal the 2001 AUMF, enforce the War Powers Resolution and oppose foreign financial commitments while domestic needs go unmet.

energy.evidence: General statement: pledges to fight policies that raise diesel, propane and electricity costs for rural producers.

notes: Read the campaign site (home, platform, about, food independence, Live Free or Die, press pages) and an InDepthNH reader forum; web search was unavailable this round. No stated positions found on immigration, education, religion, social programs or tech regulation beyond surveillance and data-center concerns.

name: Alan B. Bond
bio: Alan B. Bond is a Montclair, New Jersey resident running in NJ-11 under the Hope for Tomorrow label. He holds degrees from Dartmouth and Harvard Business School, worked at Morgan Guaranty, Goldman Sachs and W.R. Lazard, and later ran a pension management firm. He was convicted in a 2003 federal kickback case, served prison time until 2008 and paid restitution and fines.

platform.point: Wants to reduce federal tax pressure on middle-income households.
Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare.
Wants to lower prescription drug costs through more competition.
Supports secure borders, stronger legal immigration processes and more immigration court capacity.
Backs strong security cooperation with Israel alongside diplomacy that protects civilians.
Would back troop deployment only under direct threat, with clear objectives, after diplomacy and sanctions.
Calls the Gateway Tunnel essential to North Jersey and wants steady federal funding for it.

welfare.evidence: General statement: pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare.

immigration.evidence: General statement: pairs secure borders with a stronger legal immigration system and more immigration court capacity.

foreign.evidence: Backs strong security cooperation with Israel but would deploy troops only when national security is directly threatened.

notes: Positions come from his written response to the April 2026 NJ-11 special election debate reported by New Jersey Globe; no campaign website was found and web search was unavailable this round. No stated positions found on abortion, guns, policing, energy, tech, education or religion.

name: Winston Jordan
bio: Winston Jordan, 68, is a Brooklyn native living in Hopewell Township, New Jersey. He is a U.S. Army veteran who worked as a computer systems analyst, engineer and IT executive in the pharmaceutical and tech sectors. A former Democrat, he runs an independent campaign that accepts no donations and is funded from his own money.

platform.point: Pass an American Economic Security Act with a $50,000 minimum livable income guarantee.
Offer a 50-year tax holiday for the bottom 99% of earners.
Supports Medicare for All.
Run a 24/7 digital town hall letting constituents vote on congressional decisions.
Supports the Stop Act to ban members of Congress from making fundraising calls.
Proposes a federal job guarantee and a universal livable income funded partly by an automation dividend.
Wants transparency, safety testing and worker displacement reporting required for all AI systems.
Opposes war with Iran, favoring diplomacy and non-intervention, with any war decision put to a national referendum.

economy.evidence: His economic plan would fund compensation through taxes aimed at millionaires, billionaires and large corporations, plus a federal job guarantee.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and a $50,000 guaranteed minimum income.

foreign.evidence: Opposes war with Iran and calls for non-interventionism in the Middle East, and condemns the war in Gaza as genocide.

energy.evidence: General statement: calls for investment in renewable energy and clean technology as part of reindustrialization.

tech.evidence: Calls for mandatory AI transparency, safety testing and displacement reporting, data ownership rights and treating broadband as a public utility.

notes: Read the campaign site's policy text, the WHYY voter guide and Daily Princetonian forum coverage; web search was unavailable this round. No stated positions found on abortion, guns, policing, immigration, education or religion.

name: Ramon Mora Jr.
bio: Ramon Mora Jr., 31, is a Vineland resident and self-described progressive running as an independent in New Jersey's 2nd congressional district. A lifelong South Jersey resident and college graduate, he kept his ballot spot in June 2026 after Democrats dropped a challenge to his petitions.

platform.point: Supports Medicare or government health care for all and removing private insurance companies.
Describes himself as first and foremost pro-choice, backing full bodily autonomy.
Wants to abolish ICE and replace it with a new, more heavily trained federal unit.
Calls for mandatory body cameras for all police interactions and much longer officer training.
Would bar corporations from buying homes and build price-stabilized, citizen-owned housing.
Proposes no income tax on earnings under $40,000 a year and uncapping Social Security taxes.
Has urged local councils to ban or pause AI hyperscale data centers.
Opposes funding Israel's costs while Americans go without and rejects AIPAC money.

economy.evidence: Proposes government-run alternatives in essential industries, bans on bank junk fees, uncapping Social Security taxes and mandated paid leave.

welfare.evidence: Supports government health care for all, eliminating insurance companies and universal paid family leave of one to two years.

liberty.evidence: On abortion he is pro-choice with full bodily autonomy; on LGBTQ rights he says to let people be; guns, drugs and speech not addressed.

security.evidence: Calls for mandatory police body cameras, major police reform and abolishing ICE, with penalties for officer misconduct.

immigration.evidence: Wants to abolish and replace ICE and to arrest individual offenders rather than target groups.

foreign.evidence: Opposes funding Israel and backs ending forever wars, while calling for stronger ties and soft power with Western allies.

energy.evidence: Proposes expanding the grid with solar, wind, water and nuclear power on already-cleared land to cut electric bills.

tech.evidence: Backs local AI data center bans, privacy laws, right-to-repair laws and challenging monopolies.

notes: Read the campaign site's home, issues, issue detail, biography and news pages plus New Jersey Globe coverage; web search was unavailable this round. No stated positions found on education or religion in public life.

name: Seamus Patrick O'Toole
bio: Seamus Patrick O'Toole is an independent candidate for New Jersey's 7th congressional district, appearing on the ballot under the slogan "Stop Israel's Genocide." He qualified by petition, and his signatures withstood a challenge in June 2026.

platform.point: Runs on a ballot slogan centred on opposing Israel's military conduct in Gaza.

notes: Searched New Jersey Globe and tried WHYY guide paths (web search was unavailable this round); found only ballot-access coverage. No campaign website, biography or issue statements beyond the ballot slogan were found, so no scores were assigned.

name: Aristotle Eliopoulos
bio: Aristotle "Ari" Eliopoulos is a teacher and union representative running as an independent in New Jersey's 8th congressional district. A registered Republican, he filed as an independent after no Republican entered the race and has backing from local GOP leaders. He was raised in Jersey City by Greek immigrant parents who ran a small business, and was brought up in the Greek Orthodox Church.

platform.point: Wants more federal support for public schools, less standardized testing and more career and technical education.
Seeks more special education funding, early intervention and stronger IDEA protections.
Would cut taxes for working and middle-class families and expand the Child Tax Credit.
Supports workforce housing, first-time buyer incentives and a crackdown on corporate housing speculation.
Supports unions and collective bargaining, reshoring manufacturing and fewer regulations on small businesses.
Supports law enforcement with more accountability, community policing and a focus on violent repeat offenders.
Wants a modernized system with faster visa processing, legal pathways and action against trafficking and cartels.
Supports U.S. allies, closer U.S.-Greece ties and a strong national defense.

economy.evidence: General statements mix tax cuts for working families and fewer small-business regulations with support for unions and curbs on corporate housing speculation.

welfare.evidence: General statements: expand the Child Tax Credit, protect Medicare and Social Security and lower drug costs.

security.evidence: General statement: supports law enforcement and community policing while increasing accountability.

immigration.evidence: General statement: supports legal immigration pathways and faster processing alongside a 'secure borders' heading.

foreign.evidence: General statement: supports allies and strategic partnerships and a strong national defense.

education.evidence: Calls for more federal support for public schools while also listing support for parental involvement in education.

faith.evidence: General statement: platform pledges to protect religious liberty and support faith-based organizations.

notes: Read the full campaign site platform and New Jersey Globe filing coverage; web search was unavailable this round. No stated positions found on abortion, guns, energy or tech regulation.

name: Craig Honts
bio: Craig Honts is the Socialist Workers Party candidate for New Jersey's 8th congressional district. He was the party's nominee for lieutenant governor of New Jersey in 2025, running with gubernatorial candidate Joanne Kuniansky.
notes: Searched New Jersey Globe (only a filing list mention) and tried The Militant, which blocked automated access; web search was unavailable this round. No candidate-specific statements were found, and positions were not inferred from the party label.

name: Da'Shone Hughey
bio: Da'Shone Hughey is an independent candidate in New Jersey's 8th congressional district, appearing on the ballot under the "We The People" slogan.
notes: Searched New Jersey Globe, which lists only the filing; web search was unavailable this round. No campaign website, biography or public positions were found.
